title: Corrected QWOT Initialization at 425 nm with Stochastic Perturbation
scientific_hypothesis: Initializing layer thicknesses near quarter-wave optical thickness at the UV reflection band center (425 nm) rather than the SWIR transmission band will better establish the short-wavelength stopband, and stochastic perturbation will help escape higher-order resonance local minima that limited prior rounds.
design_principle: Quarter-wave stack design with HfO2/SiO2 alternating layers, initialized at λ0=425 nm QWOT values (HfO2≈53 nm, SiO2≈73 nm for n≈2.0 and n≈1.46), with ±15% uniform random noise added to break symmetry and enable optimizer to traverse between optical resonances.
proposed_topology: Air | [HfO2 | SiO2]×8 | Fused Silica substrate (16 finite layers total, 8 high-index and 8 low-index layers in alternating sequence starting with HfO2)
design_variables: 16 layer physical thicknesses in nm, initialized near 425 nm QWOT with ±15% noise, optimization bounds relaxed by 25% from prior rounds
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count 16 is well within 30-layer fabrication limit
Individual layer thicknesses 40-100 nm range is compatible with standard deposition monitoring
HfO2/SiO2 material pair has established deposition processes for low stress and high laser damage threshold
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for plane-wave propagation through isotropic layered media
Quarter-wave stack theory: stopband centered at wavelength where optical thickness equals λ/4
Higher-order resonance avoidance through randomized initialization
expected_advantages: Better UV stopband establishment through proper QWOT initialization at reflection band
Escaping local minima through stochastic perturbation
Relaxed bounds allow optimizer to explore thickness space between lower and higher order resonances
known_risks: Optimizer may still converge to suboptimal local minimum despite perturbation
16 layers may be insufficient for both wide UV stopband and wide SWIR passband simultaneously
Index dispersion not fully captured in single-wavelength QWOT estimate
execution_request_english: Optimize a 16-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 dielectric stack on fused silica substrate under normal air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2 (16 finite layers total). Initialize thicknesses at quarter-wave optical thickness for 425 nm center wavelength (HfO2 nominal 53 nm, SiO2 nominal 73 nm) with ±15% uniform random noise applied to each layer. Set optimization bounds: HfO2 layers 35-120 nm, SiO2 layers 50-150 nm. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with dual-band objective: maximize mean transmittance over 1000-1700 nm and maximize mean reflectance over 300-450 nm, equal weighting. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized or average of TE and TM. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates count, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all valid candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: reflection in 1000-1700 nm; transmission in 300-450 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count <= 30.
revision_reason: Reset thickness initialization from SWIR-centered (~100-200 nm) to UV-centered QWOT (~50-75 nm) per feedback directive to better establish the 300-450 nm reflection stopband. Added ±15% stochastic perturbation to break higher-order mode lock observed in prior rounds. Relaxed thickness upper bounds by 25% to enable optimizer traversal between optical resonances.
